vignette: Lena, a 35-year-old African woman and a dedicated tutor, has been struggling immensely since a traumatic incident that occurred three months ago. The event was a violent rape during one of her late-night tutoring sessions in a dimly lit library on campus. Since then, Lena's life has been irrevocably altered by the haunting memories and debilitating symptoms she experiences. The night of the assault is seared into Lena's memory with terrifying clarity. She had stayed late at the library to help a struggling student finish an important project. As she was walking back to her car in the parking lot, someone approached her from behind, overpowering her before she could react. The fear and horror of that moment have left lasting imprints on her psyche. Since then, Lena has found herself triggered by the most unexpected sounds, such as children crying nearby or even hearing a child's voice over the phone. Each time she hears these cries, it sets off a wave of panic, bringing back the overwhelming terror she experienced during the assault. The uncertainty that follows each trigger only exacerbates her distress, leaving her feeling helpless and unable to control her reactions. Lena has also begun experiencing nausea whenever she thinks about the event or encounters anything that reminds her of it. This somatic response adds another layer of discomfort, making her feel like she is perpetually on edge. She often finds herself avoiding situations where these triggers might be present, such as family gatherings or social events with friends. In addition to these triggers, Lena has been ruminating excessively about the assault and repeatedly blaming herself for what happened. She questions whether she could have done something differently to prevent it, feeling guilty and responsible despite having no control over the situation. This self-blame has led her to avoid positive experiences that might make her feel hopeful or happy, as any sense of well-being is quickly overshadowed by the memories of the trauma. Lena also avoids reminders of the event, whether they come from others or herself. She finds it particularly distressing when someone else brings up details about that night, causing her to withdraw and isolate herself further. This has strained her relationships, including her romantic partnership, where she struggles to open up and share what she is going through. The memory of the assault feels alien to Lena; it doesn't feel like something that happened to her but rather to someone else. Each time she tries to recall the event, the same terror washes over her, making it nearly impossible for her to put the experience into words. This nonverbal memory makes it difficult for her to seek help or express what she is going through. Lena's negative appraisals are deeply entrenched. She believes that she has been permanently changed for the worse and doubts her ability to cope with any sort of upset, no matter how slight. The thought of having to face these memories head-on terrifies her, leading her to avoid thinking about them altogether. However, this avoidance only serves to heighten her anxiety and make it harder to engage in normal activities. Over time, Lena's symptoms have taken a toll on her professional life as well. Her tutoring sessions, once a source of joy and fulfillment, now feel like a burden. She finds herself canceling appointments frequently due to the overwhelming fear that any small trigger might set off an episode. This has led to strained relationships with her students and colleagues, further isolating her from the very support system she needs. What finally brought Lena to seek help was the realization that she could no longer function in her daily life without some form of intervention. Her avoidance behaviors had become so severe that even simple tasks like grocery shopping or going out for a walk felt overwhelming. She is most afraid of reliving the trauma and being unable to handle it, yet she hopes for a way to regain control over her life and find peace with her past. In seeking help, Lena hopes to navigate through these fears and build resilience against the triggers that have dominated her life since the assault. She yearns for a future where she can look back on this experience without being consumed by it, but instead, be able to move forward with a sense of strength and healing.
